speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) whether there are claims filed with the Financial Dispute Resolution Centre which involve an unauthorised bank transaction reportedly taking place and the bank has assessed that the One-Time Password (OTP) SMS messaging was used, but the customer's telephone operator records do not show transmission or receipt of such SMS OTP; and (b) whether there are other avenues available for these customers to seek redress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: When customers suspect that they have fallen for a scam or are alerted by the bank to unauthorised transactions involving their account, they should immediately contact the bank or activate the kill switch that the banks provide to freeze their accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: They should also report such fraudulent activities to the Police.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The banks must consider, one, whether they have fulfilled their obligations, and two, whether customers have done their part to protect their accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Depending on the outcome of the banks’ investigations, they may offer goodwill payment to customers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Is there a process for having this review besides FIDReC or does the bank have the final say on this question?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: A year ago, in February 2022, I asked in Parliament about the risk of emerging deepfake audio and video calls.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Since then, there have been potential cases in the United States of deepfake audio voice calls.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Minister whether the proposed equitable framework for sharing of losses will look at such emerging risks and will it also consider my previous suggestion on the difference between a customer making a forced error – for example, with a deepfake – versus an unforced error?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We know that the techniques employed by scammers are constantly evolving and also gaining in sophistication with the use of differentiated technologies and this also thus requires a multi-pronged response across our ecosystem to strengthen our collective mechanisms and resilience against scams.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) will continue to work closely with our ecosystem partners, including the banking industry and other Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, MAS is working with banks to allow customers to verify genuine calls from banks.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Members of the public can also play their part.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Please install Scamshield; do not divulge your Internet banking credentials or passwords to anyone; be suspicious of unsolicited messages or calls that you receive and also verify calls received by calling the bank directly on the hotline listed on the official websites or cards.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For the first question, I will refer the Member to my main reply to the Parliamentary Question (PQ).

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But for the questions with regard to the equitable sharing of losses, Dr Lim Wee Kiat has filed a PQ on that matter for this Sitting and we will address this issue in response to that PQ.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Gerald Giam, a very short clarification or supplementary question because we are going to be running out of Question Time very soon.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Clarification by the Minister of State Sun Xueling.
